Create a documentary reportage photograph of a woman in her late thirties, a Sports World member, standing still in a training room, frozen mid-breath one second after finishing a set. Head and shoulders, three-quarter framing, eyes straight on the lens. Her face is irregular, not symmetrical: a nose with a visible bump on the bridge, a thin pale scar cutting through the left eyebrow, deep-set eyes, one brow sitting slightly higher than the other, dark hair pulled back tight with two loose strands stuck to her damp temple. Skin is documented, not flattered: red patches across the cheeks, faint flaking at the crease of the nostril, uneven pigment on the forehead, sweat collecting above the upper lip, individual fine hairs along the jaw, cracked lips, open pores across the nose. Wearing a charcoal training t-shirt with a black wristband on the left wrist. Hard light: one single hard source raking in from camera-left, no fill, so every pore throws its own shadow and the texture of the skin reads at full size. Background is the room dropping into darkness, a rubber floor and a rack of iron plates far out of focus. Kodak Tri-X reportage look, natural contrast, visible grain in the shadows, no HDR look. Anti-beauty rules: no beauty retouching, no skin smoothing, no even complexion, no soft fill light. Fine detail at 100 percent: pores, fabric weave of the collar, stray hairs against the light. Format: 4:5.
